name: Learn and Be Curious
definition: Leaders are never done learning and always seek to improve themselves. They are curious about new possibilities and act to explore them.

rows.situation: You tried a new planning process and missed the deadline
rows.under: Blames the people, not the process. Forces the old process on the next project.
rows.justRight: Talks to the people who used it. Keeps what worked and adjusts what did not. Tries the improved version next time.
rows.over: Throws the process out and tries a third one.

rows.situation: One customer report contradicts a positive aggregate
rows.under: Calls it a rounding error. Ignores the single report because the overall response looks fine.
rows.justRight: Digs in. Finds what went wrong and what it will take to fix.
rows.over: Launches a three-month study aimed at that one issue.

rows.situation: A teammate makes a mistake that takes the site down
rows.under: Puts up a wall of shame so nobody ever makes that mistake again.
rows.justRight: Changes the system so that class of mistake cannot happen, or cannot have the same blast radius.
rows.over: Insists everyone must personally experience the mistake as training.

rows.situation: Someone learns a useful technique on a project
rows.under: Uses it on their project and stops.
rows.justRight: Writes it down and teaches it in a short team session so others can use it.
rows.over: Makes the technique mandatory training for the whole team.

rows.situation: The team needs a new data store
rows.under: Insists on the one technology everyone already knows.
rows.justRight: Researches options, prototypes the top two or three, and takes the findings to a design review.
rows.over: Prototypes every available option and stress-tests all of them before anyone can choose.
